subject: pe
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the skeletal system?
questions.explain: Gaseous exchange occurs in the lungs, whereas the skeleton provides support, protection, movement and produces blood cells.

questions.q: The femur (thigh bone) is classified as which type of bone?
questions.explain: The femur is a long bone, which acts as a lever to allow large, powerful movements.

questions.q: When the biceps contracts to flex the elbow, which muscle acts as the antagonist?
questions.explain: In an antagonistic pair the biceps is the agonist (prime mover) and the triceps is the relaxing antagonist during elbow flexion.

questions.q: What type of synovial joint is found at the knee?
questions.explain: The knee is a hinge joint, allowing flexion and extension in one plane only.

questions.q: Where in the lungs does gaseous exchange take place?
questions.explain: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged across the thin walls of the alveoli and surrounding capillaries.

questions.q: Which type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
questions.explain: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure, while veins return blood to the heart.

questions.q: Which statement best describes anaerobic exercise?
options: High-intensity exercise without sufficient oxygen, producing lactic acid
Low-intensity exercise using plenty of oxygen
Steady exercise lasting more than 30 minutes
Exercise that only uses the aerobic energy system
questions.explain: Anaerobic exercise is short, high-intensity work performed without enough oxygen, resulting in a build-up of lactic acid.

questions.q: Which is a long-term effect of aerobic training on the cardiovascular system?
options: Increased breathing rate during a single session
questions.explain: Regular aerobic training causes the heart muscle to grow larger and stronger, increasing stroke volume and lowering resting heart rate.

questions.q: In a first-class lever, where is the fulcrum located?
options: Between the effort and the load
At the same point as the load
Beyond both the effort and the load
Between the load and the muscle only
questions.explain: In a first-class lever the fulcrum lies between the effort and the load, as seen when nodding the head at the neck.

questions.q: Which action in the body is an example of a second-class lever?
options: Standing up on tiptoes (plantar flexion at the ankle)
Nodding the head at the neck
questions.explain: Rising onto the toes is a second-class lever, with the load positioned between the fulcrum and the effort.

questions.q: A gymnast performs a forward somersault. In which plane and around which axis does this movement occur?
questions.explain: A forward somersault is a rotation in the sagittal plane around the frontal axis.

questions.q: An ice skater performs a spinning full twist. In which plane and around which axis does this occur?
questions.explain: A twist or spin is a rotation in the transverse plane around the longitudinal (vertical) axis.

questions.q: What do the letters in the FITT principle stand for?
questions.explain: FITT stands for Frequency, Intensity, Time and Type, and is used to apply progressive overload.

questions.q: Which fitness test measures aerobic endurance (cardiovascular fitness)?
questions.explain: The multi-stage fitness (bleep) test assesses aerobic endurance by predicting VO2 max.

questions.q: Which component of fitness does the sit and reach test measure?
questions.explain: The sit and reach test measures flexibility, mainly in the lower back and hamstrings.

questions.q: Using the formula 220 minus age, what is the estimated maximum heart rate of a 15-year-old?
questions.explain: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 minus age, so 220 - 15 = 205 bpm.

questions.q: Which principle of training involves gradually increasing the amount of overload over time?
questions.explain: Progressive overload means gradually increasing training demands so the body continues to adapt and improve.

questions.q: Data collected as numerical measurements, such as heart rate in beats per minute, is known as:
questions.explain: Quantitative data is numerical and objective, such as times, distances or heart rates.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes qualitative data?
options: Non-numerical information based on descriptions or opinions
Data measured with a stopwatch or tape measure
Data that can only be shown on a bar chart
questions.explain: Qualitative data is descriptive and subjective, for example judging the quality of a performer's technique.

questions.q: A coach wants to show how an athlete's resting heart rate has changed over eight weeks of training. Which is the most suitable way to present this data?
options: Single data table with no headings
questions.explain: A line graph is best for showing continuous change in a variable, such as heart rate, over time.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE PE & Sport Science (1PE0) specification; Fitness and Body Systems
